case: A trigger session-variable side effect survives rollback of a failed InnoDB batch
contract: An AFTER INSERT trigger increments a connection-scoped MySQL user variable.
The first batch INSERT fires the trigger; a later duplicate-key INSERT fails and causes rollback.
The InnoDB row from the failed batch is absent after rollback.
The trigger's user-variable increment remains visible on the same connection after rollback.
remaining: This is one confirmed side-effect type in the MySQL 8.1 fixture; other engines and external side effects remain untested.
Frozen-candidate and hosted acceptance remain open.
